A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GATEAU study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v6 reports original model evaluations, ablations, human judgments, retrieval tests, and additional appendix experiments.

after.justification: v7 retains these original empirical results in its main text and appendices.

M1.justification: HMG, CAM, their weighted scoring combination, sample selection, and supervised fine-tuning remain unchanged. Equations (1)-(7) specify the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain LongAlign and ShareGPT training, additional LongAlpaca experiments, LongBench, LongBench-Chat, MT-Bench, retrieval tests, and the debate case study. The expanded main-text LongAlign description already appears in v6 Appendix A.

E2.justification: Perplexity Guidance, CaR, Cherry Selection, and the full-data and no-SFT controls retain their membership in corresponding comparisons. Appendix comparators also remain unchanged; shortening the Cherry Selection description does not establish a procedural revision.

E3.justification: Data mixtures, selection ratios, model configurations, training budgets, truncation, metrics, and evaluation procedures are retained. Human-evaluation tie-breaking and the retrieval setup shown in v7 Section 3.3 were already documented in v6 Appendices E and F.

E4.justification: The component, scalability, parameter-sensitivity, diversity, HMG, in-context alignment, mixed-quality, and case-study analyses are retained. Moving the Needle-in-a-Haystack analysis into the main text adds no new analysis or evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain averaging two GPT-4 scorings, including the 200-sample assessment in Appendix D. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or removed.

E6.justification: All 15 tables retain identical corresponding entries after matching v6 Tables 14 and 15 to v7 Tables 15 and 14. Plotted results and appendix case-study outputs are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The score definitions, training objective, and appendix mathematical expressions are unchanged. Summation typesetting changes do not alter the mathematics, and no new assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contribution: selecting influential long-context samples through complementary dependency-related scores to improve alignment with less training data.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, data quantity-quality interpretation, and three substantive limitations remain. The 30% selection explanation added to the main text already appears in v6 Appendix C.2; other edits largely paraphrase existing interpretations.

D1.justification: v7 omits the literal retrieval prompt printed in v6 Appendix F, retaining only its attribution. The first-page release statement drops models from the promised data, code, and models, and adds a contact email. These are disclosure changes, not evidence of changed actual resource availability.

R1.justification: v7 adds UltraIF and four Si et al. papers, while removing citations to GLM, positional interpolation, Stanford Alpaca, and How Far Can Camels Go? The distinction between earlier short-instruction selection and GATEAU's long-context focus remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v7 integrates former Appendices E and F into Section 3.3, renumbers subsequent appendices, shortens the Cherry Selection explanation, and repeats existing background in the main text. It also revises author affiliations and adds acknowledgements; most prose and the overall narrative remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 5 moves from the appendix to the main text, parameter plots are repositioned, and Tables 14 and 15 exchange order. The title's cake icon is removed and equation typography changes. Existing scientific displays retain their content and structure.

improvement.justification: v7 makes existing analyses more visible and modestly streamlines explanations, while retaining the same method, experimental evidence, and substantive limitations. These limited presentation benefits, alongside the omitted retrieval prompt and narrower release disclosure, leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
